title.narrative: Provisions of life-saving WASH assistance to drought-affected and displaced vulnerable communities, in under-served and hard-to-reach areas in Beletweyne.

description.narrative: ltpgtDaryeel Bulsho Guud (DBG) proposes a 10-month WASH intervention to address urgent humanitarian needs among internally displaced persons (IDPs) and flood-affected rural populations in Beletweyne District, Hiraan Region. The project targets 20,210 people, including 9,940 women, 2,525 girls, 5,220 men, and 2,525 boys in Doomey and Barwaqo IDP settlements and the rural villages of Shabelow and Ilko-ade.lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtThe intervention is informed by DBG’s June 2025 assessment, which revealed that 91% of households rely on unsafe river water, 72% of latrines were destroyed by floods, and hygiene supplies are virtually unavailable. The project aims to reduce WASH-related disease and mortality through a multi-pronged response that includes rehabilitation of 10 shallow wells, and 1 high yield shallow well, Standalone chlorination of water points, provision of essential spare part kits for the wells, a total of 22 spare part kits will be procured and distributed to the 15 trained Water User Committees (WUCs) established at each water point. Additionally, DBG will onduct training for 15 water management committees (WMC), and construction of 50 gender-sensitive and disability-inclusive emergency latrines. Additionally, 30 sanitation tool-kits will be distributed 48 weeks of hygiene promotion. Six handwashing stations will be installed at two health facilities to strengthen infection prevention and control (IPC), and 12 damaged latrines in IDP sites will be rehabilitated. Monthly community-led cleaning campaigns and a local radio awareness campaign will reinforce behavior change and safe sanitation practices. Further, distribute 900 hygiene kits to flood-affected households to prevent disease outbreaks.Each kit includes aqua tabs, jerry can, bucket, soap, and menstrual hygiene items, per WASH standards.clt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe project aligns with the 2025 SHF First Standard Allocation Strategy and the WASH Cluster objectives, prioritizing protection, gender and disability inclusion, and accountability to affected populations. DBG’s deep roots in Beletweyne and proven WASH delivery capacity make it well-positioned to respond rapidly and effectively to one of Somalia’s most undeserved humanitarian crises.ltbrgtlt/pgt
